story.see: The Niebla fire was declared on a Thursday, probably 6 August 2026, in the province of Huelva and crossed into Seville; by 13 August it had burned more than 31,000 hectares, with a perimeter of about 120 km (Infobae). The orange area is where the radar picture between NISAR's 21 July and 14 August passes no longer matches the pair taken just before it (9 to 21 July). It forms a wide sharp-edged block north-east of Niebla.
story.physics: Burning removes the leaves, twigs and scrub that gave this dry hill country a repeatable radar echo. About 218 km2 in the map lost coherence (110 km2 within 15 km of the centre); equal circles elsewhere lose at most 29 km2. The ascending pass shows the same block (145 km2 within 15 km), and the pair of 14 to 26 August shows nothing. The north edge of the scar is almost straight over 25 km at the same latitude (37.57 to 37.61 N) in both passes, so it is a feature of the ground, not of the radar frame; we did not identify it. We do not measure the burned area.
story.lband: NISAR's L-band radar has a wavelength of about 24 cm. Here the pair is 24 days long while the control is 12, which lowers coherence everywhere a little; the control is bright almost everywhere and the scar stays dark with hard edges. Rain or dew on the ground cannot be fully excluded from coherence alone; the shape, the place and the date are what we rely on.
story.people: This map shows where the surface changed, not damage. We did not look at reports of damage, evacuations or casualties.
